messages:
daniel_cust: Hey team — after moving Redwood Private into our VPC we're seeing model pulls fail: TLS handshake error when contacting model-registry.redwood.ai from our onprem nodes. We use split-horizon DNS (internal resolves to internal-proxy.example.com). Can you confirm what egress hosts/ports we must allow? Also our proxy rewrites SNI which may break cert pinning :disappointed:

maria_support: Sorry for the trouble. Can you paste the exact error and a `curl -v` output from one of the nodes? Also let us know if there's a transparent TLS intercepting proxy in the path.

daniel_cust: Here's the `curl -v` output from the app server:
```
curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/models/abc -o /dev/null
* Connected to internal-proxy.example.com (10.10.10.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 handshake, Certificate verif failed: certificate has expired
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
```
We do have an outbound TLS proxy that performs TLS rewrap and SNI rewrite.

siva_infra: That output looks like TLS interception. For Private deployments we expect either SNI passthrough for our hostnames or a proxy that can present certs chained to your root and preserve original SNI.

jenna_eng: Also double-check OCSP/CRL access — some proxies block OCSP requests which will surface as cert verification failures during handshakes.

maria_support: To unblock quickly, please ensure egress TCP/443 to these FQDNs (minimum):
- registry.redwood-infra.com
- models-cdn.redwood.ai
- telemetry-ingest.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
And allow outbound DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your resolver. If you're using split-horizon and the resolver returns internal proxy addresses, you may need to allow outbound to resolver.redwood.ai:53 so our control-plane lookups succeed. If you cannot allow SNI passthrough, add the above CNs/CNs as exceptions in your TLS proxy.

daniel_cust: Our security team wants CIDR ranges, not FQDNs. Any recommended IP blocks?

siva_infra: We run behind multiple CDNs so we strongly recommend FQDN allowlisting. As a temporary measure you can open these example prefixes: 34.120.0.0/14, 52.23.128.0/17, 3.210.0.0/15 — but please treat them as non-exhaustive. We'll produce a signed, canonical CIDR list for your ops team.

deploy-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1024 — support lead assigned: maria_support

maria_support: I'll upload a KB with the canonical allowlist and a short troubleshooting checklist (SNI passthrough, OCSP, DNS split-horizon hints). Meanwhile can you run `openssl s_client -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -connect internal-proxy.example.com:443` and paste the peer cert subject?

daniel_cust: Quick `openssl` dump: peer cert subject shows `subject=/CN=internal-proxy` — so proxy is rewriting the cert CN. We'll try to add exception rules for those hostnames. Thanks, will update.

oncall-ml: FYI — model download auth flows also call a token exchange endpoint. If you see repeated 401s, allow outbound to auth-token.redwood.ai:443 (separate from model registry).

maria_support: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the formal allowlist and a one-line firewall checklist. If you hit anything after adding exceptions, ping me and we'll get an engineer to reproduce inside your VPC.
